q.t: Of all the dispositions and habits which lead to political prosperity, Religion and morality are indispensable supports.
Those who would give up essential Liberty, to purchase a little temporary Safety, deserve neither Liberty nor Safety.
q.s: Pennsylvania Assembly: Reply to the Governor, November 11, 1755

q.t: I have sworn upon the altar of god eternal hostility against every form of tyranny over the mind of man.
Our Constitution was made only for a moral and religious People. It is wholly inadequate to the government of any other.
q.s: Letter to the Massachusetts Militia, October 11, 1798

q.t: Liberty, when it begins to take root, is a plant of rapid growth.
The judiciary... has no influence over either the sword or the purse.
A popular Government, without popular information, or the means of acquiring it, is but a Prologue to a Farce or a Tragedy; or perhaps both.
q.s: Letter to William T. Barry, August 4, 1822

q.t: Providence has been pleased to give this one connected country to one united people.
...the Constitution which at any time exists, 'till changed by an explicit and authentic act of the whole People, is sacredly obligatory upon all.
The tree of liberty must be refreshed from time to time with the blood of patriots and tyrants.
q.s: Letter to William S. Smith, November 13, 1787

q.t: An Ounce of Prevention is worth a Pound of Cure.
q.s: On Protection of Towns from Fire, February 4, 1735

q.t: The sacred rights of mankind are not to be rummaged for, among old parchments, or musty records.
Liberty cannot be preserved without a general knowledge among the people...
q.s: A Dissertation on the Canon and the Feudal Law, 1765

q.t: Conscience is the most sacred of all property.
...nations in general will make war whenever they have a prospect of getting any thing by it...
I cannot live without books.
To be prepared for war is one of the most effectual means of preserving peace.
q.s: First Annual Message to Congress, January 8, 1790

q.t: Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy wealthy and wise.
The Religion then of every man must be left to the conviction and conscience of every man...
q.s: Memorial and Remonstrance against Religious Assessments, 1785

q.t: Energy in the Executive is a leading character in the definition of good government.
I must study Politicks and War that my sons may have liberty to study Mathematicks and Philosophy.
...a little rebellion now and then is a good thing...
Among the many objects to which a wise and free people find it necessary to direct their attention, that of providing for their safety seems to be the first.
It is better to offer no excuse than a bad one.
Well done is better than well said.
A well instructed people alone can be permanently a free people.
Why has government been instituted at all? Because the passions of men will not conform to the dictates of reason and justice, without constraint.
The only maxim of a free government ought to be to trust no man living with power to endanger the public liberty.
q.s: Notes for an Oration at Braintree, 1772

q.t: When angry, count ten, before you speak; if very angry, an hundred.
q.s: Letter to Thomas Jefferson Smith, February 21, 1825

q.t: Discipline is the soul of an army.
Liberty once lost is lost forever.
Remember that time is money.
